findings.text: Cache flag resolver kmem_cache_flags takes caller flags plus cache name and yields effective flags after applying global debug defaults and optional name-pattern overrides; one build variant performs this selection while an alternate build passes flags through unchanged.

Cache teardown entry __kmem_cache_release releases auxiliary state in fixed order covering randomization storage, per-CPU sheaf structures, per-CPU statistics when that build option is present, and per-node metadata.

Randomization-table creator cache_random_seq_create ensures a shuffled index table exists for later freelist ordering; one build provides a working allocator-backed implementation while a header variant reports success without action.
Randomization-table destructor cache_random_seq_destroy releases the table and clears the cache pointer; a header variant is a no-op for builds without randomization support.

Mergeability queries slab_args_unmergeable and slab_unmergeable report whether creation arguments or a live cache forbid merging, based on global opt-out slab_nomerge, constructor presence, hardening-related usersize, never-merge marking, and bootstrap refcount state.
Size-rounding helper kmalloc_size_roundup maps a request length to the bucket object_size for small requests, to a page-multiple for mid-range requests, and leaves zero or oversize inputs unchanged.

Flag resolution leaves inputs untouched when marker SLAB_NO_USER_FLAGS is present; caches marked SLAB_NOLEAKTRACE do not inherit SLAB_STORE_USER from global defaults slub_debug; otherwise a first matching name block contributes its flags, and with no match the global defaults are merged in.

Debug option language accepts empty blocks, leading-comma defaults via DEBUG_DEFAULT_FLAGS, single letters with f for consistency checks SLAB_CONSISTENCY_CHECKS, z for red zoning SLAB_RED_ZONE, p for poisoning SLAB_POISON, u for user tracking SLAB_STORE_USER, t for tracing SLAB_TRACE, a for fault injection SLAB_FAILSLAB, o for higher-order suppression recorded in disable_higher_order_debug during init, and dash for clear, plus optional comma-introduced name lists with glob matching and block chaining.

Cache randomization setup init_cache_random_seq is idempotent when random_seq already exists, creates a table sized by per-slab object count, and converts entries from indexes into byte offsets using final size stride; creation is skipped for tiny counts or existing tables, with a no-op build variant.
Initializer freelist_randomize fills the table with identity positions and then applies an in-place unbiased shuffle driven by a bounded uniform random source with pairwise exchanges.

Setup helper alloc_kmem_cache_stats validates at build time that early dynamic per-CPU space can hold all bucket-type counters, then allocates a per-CPU statistics area cpu_stats and signals presence of the area through its outcome.

Per-CPU sheaf setup init_percpu_sheaves gives every possible processor a lock plus a main sheaf pointer that is always valid; zero-capacity caches share a single immutable empty bootstrap sheaf with no owning cache, while other caches receive freshly allocated empty sheaves, with allocation failure aborting setup.

Release unwinding tolerates partially constructed caches by skipping absent per-CPU areas cpu_sheaves and absent sheaf pointers, freeing only empty main sheaves and per-node barns and node objects after prior shutdown flushing.

Node bring-up requires early slab path while boot state is down and node-cache path once up, with per-node barns present only after boot when sheaves are active; any allocation shortage aborts cleanly with failure signaled.

Node and barn initializers establish empty list state with cleared counters; node setup also prepares its list lock list_lock and partial queue, while barn setup prepares its own lock and separate full and empty sheaf queues.

Early node allocation yields a privately owned node carved from a fresh slab of the dedicated node cache with single-object use accounted and partial queuing, requiring no locking because the structure is not yet shareable.

Object layout guarantees word-aligned payload with in-use length inuse recorded before growth, freelist link kept outside object for unsafe reclamation, construction, poisoning or small red-zone cases and otherwise placed centrally or at explicit offset, with tracking, sanitizer and alignment growth applied before order selection and page-modifier mapping, succeeding only when at least one object fits.

Slab order choice derives minimum object count from configuration or processor-count heuristic, clamps it to achievable maximum, enforces per-page object ceiling, then scans upward orders for acceptable waste starting strict and progressively relaxing, falling back to single-object order when necessary, with sizing packed via oo_make.

Sheaf capacity calculate_sheaf_capacity is disabled for tiny builds, debug-marked caches SLAB_DEBUG_FLAGS, bootstrap caches SLAB_NO_SHEAVES and leak-tracing-exempt caches SLAB_NOLEAKTRACE; otherwise a size-tiered base value is grown to fill a malloc bucket exactly and raised to honor an explicit minimum sheaf_capacity request.

Bucket lookup kmalloc_slab derives cache type from allocation context, forces a no-extension type when extension suppression is requested, defaults the bucket table, and selects by indexed table for small sizes or by most-significant-bit position for larger sizes, with tiny sizes mapped through eight-byte steps via size_index_elem.

Sysfs publication treats caches as unmergeable when global or per-cache policy forbids merging or when higher-order debug suppression meets metadata debugging; unmergeable caches publish under true name after clearing stale links while mergeable caches use generated unique names plus a name alias, tolerating registration failure to allow creation to proceed.

Barn and cache-node list protection use spin locks initialized during creation via lock and list_lock fields; per-CPU sheaf structures use local try-locks initialized for every processor; early node creation performs no locking because the new node is not yet shareable.
Node barn holdings comprise guarding lock, distinct queues sheaves_full and sheaves_empty for full and empty sheaves, and counters nr_full and nr_empty tracking occupancy of each queue.
Cache-node state comprises partial tally nr_partial, guard list_lock, queue partial, and in debug builds tallies nr_slabs and total_objects plus queue full.

Per-processor sheaf holder comprises local lock with pointers main, spare and rcu_free; each sheaf tracks current occupancy size against capacity limit, objects array storage, and owning-cache link null solely for shared bootstrap instance.

Order-objects value packs slab order with object count; cache retains size stride, object_size base, inuse length, offset link position, align requirement, allocflags page modifiers, oo operational sizing and min minimal sizing, plus random_seq table, cpu_sheaves area, cpu_stats area and per_node vectors.
Node bring-up follows boot-phase state with down using early slab path and skipping barns, and up allocating nodes from node cache and then barns when sheaves are active.

Main sheaf pointer moves from absent during failed creation, to shared bootstrap for zero-capacity or debug or early cases, to dedicated empty sheaf for normal operation, and back to absent after teardown release.

Debug specification parsing walks semicolon-separated blocks each holding option letters plus optional comma-introduced name list with glob support, advancing block to block until input is exhausted, with first name match winning.
Release routine serves as terminal cache-lifecycle entry after shutdown flushing, consolidating all auxiliary frees that destroy must perform.
Flag resolver serves as creation-time policy entry merging caller flags with global and name-specific debug selections before layout proceeds.

Teardown warns when per-CPU spare or deferred pointers remain, when main sheaf still holds objects, or when per-node barn counters remain non-zero, leaving such state leaked rather than freeing inconsistently.

Early bring-up treats undersized node cache, failed slab creation, or missing first object as fatal, and logs but continues with potentially misplaced node structure when allocated slab resides on unexpected node.

Sysfs registration must handle duplicate names for unmergeable caches and allocation failure for generated names, and deliberately avoids extra reference drops so cache creation can proceed despite publication errors.

Slab debug vocabulary includes SLAB_NO_USER_FLAGS for bypass, SLAB_NOLEAKTRACE for leak-trace exemption, SLAB_CONSISTENCY_CHECKS for checks, SLAB_RED_ZONE for guard areas, SLAB_POISON for fill, SLAB_STORE_USER for caller tracking, SLAB_TRACE for tracing, SLAB_FAILSLAB for fault injection, SLAB_NEVER_MERGE for merge veto, SLAB_NO_SHEAVES for sheaf veto and SLAB_DEBUG_FLAGS as debug aggregate.

Slab placement and lifecycle vocabulary includes SLAB_RECLAIM_ACCOUNT for reclaim accounting, SLAB_CACHE_DMA and SLAB_CACHE_DMA32 for placement, SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU for deferred reclamation, SLAB_KMALLOC for bucket marking, and allocation aggregates SLAB_ALLOC_DEFAULT and SLAB_ALLOC_NO_OBJ_EXT; cache-to-page mapping always requests compound pages with DMA and reclaimable modifiers added per cache marking.

Object-state vocabulary includes internal poison marker __OBJECT_POISON applied only when poisoning is safe, and SLAB_OBJ_EXT_IN_OBJ for in-object extension embedding when merge policy and spare space allow.
